feedback.worked_solution:
A typical three-dimensional type I region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096328/assets/05f940e247c6cd5d862d81fc3a34658353bef5513dfe862bbc67a120c0345838.png)

First, the projection $D$ of the solid onto the $xy$-plane gives the domain

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2}.
$$

Next, we have

- the *bottom* surface $z={f}_{1}(x,y)=0,$ and

- the *top* surface $z={f}_{2}(x,y)=4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096328/assets/69faebe379efc8a012346b8aba235edca8e9d5adabd3bb52b5009c20d73de655.png)

Therefore, 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,0\le z\le 4\,}.
$$
